question_image.description: Structures of different isomeric amines corresponding to the molecular formula CH₄N.

parts.part_text: Write structures of different isomeric amines corresponding to the molecular formula, CH₄N.
parts.answer_text: The structures of different isomeric amines are: (a) Butanamine, (b) Butan-2-amine, (c) 2-Methylpropanamine, (d) 2-Methylpropan-2-amine, (e) N-Methylpropanamine, (f) N-Ethylethanamine.
parts.final_answer: These structures represent the isomeric amines for the given molecular formula.

parts.part_text: Write IUPAC names of all the isomers.
parts.answer_text: The IUPAC names are: (a) Butanamine, (b) Butan-2-amine, (c) 2-Methylpropanamine, (d) 2-Methylpropan-2-amine, (e) N-Methylpropanamine, (f) N-Ethylethanamine.
parts.final_answer: These are the IUPAC names of the isomeric amines.

parts.part_text: What type of isomerism is exhibited by different pairs of amines?
parts.answer_text: The pairs (a) and (b) and (e) and (g) exhibit position isomerism. The pairs (a) and (c); (a) and (d); (b) and (c); (b) and (d) exhibit chain isomerism. The pairs (e) and (f) and (f) and (g) exhibit metamerism. All primary amines exhibit functional isomerism with secondary and tertiary amines and vice-versa.
parts.final_answer: These types of isomerism are exhibited by the different pairs of amines.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of isomerism and structural representation.

question_text: Complete the following acid-base reactions and name the products: (i) CH3CH2CH2NH2 + HCl (ii) (C2H5)3N + HCl
answer_text: (i) CH3CH2CH2NH2 + HCl → CH3CH2CH2NH3Cl (n-Propylammonium chloride) (ii) (C2H5)3N + HCl → (C2H5)3NHCl (Triethylammonium chloride)
final_answer: Thus, the products are n-Propylammonium chloride and Triethylammonium chloride.

question_text:
Account for the following:
(i) pK of aniline is more than that of methylamine.
(ii) Ethylamine is soluble in water whereas aniline is not.
(iii) Methylamine in water reacts with ferric chloride to precipitate hydrated ferric oxide.
(iv) Although amino group is o, p- directing in aromatic electrophilic substitution reactions, aniline on nitration gives a substantial amount of m-nitroaniline.
(v) Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.
(vi) Diazonium salts of aromatic amines are more stable than those of aliphatic amines.
(vii) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is preferred for synthesising primary amines.

parts.part_text: pK of aniline is more than that of methylamine.
parts.answer_text: Aniline undergoes resonance and as a result, the electrons on the N-atom are delocalized over the benzene ring. Therefore, the electrons on the N-atom are less available to donate. On the other hand, in case of methylamine (due to the +I effect of methyl group), the electron density on the N-atom is increased. As a result, aniline is less basic than methylamine. Thus, pK of aniline is more than that of methylamine.

steps.description: Explain resonance in aniline and its effect on basicity.
Discuss the +I effect of the methyl group in methylamine.

parts.final_answer: Thus, pK of aniline is more than that of methylamine.

answer_images.description: Mathematical representation related to the properties of amines.

parts.part_text: Ethylamine is soluble in water whereas aniline is not.
parts.answer_text: Ethylamine when added to water forms intermolecular H-bonds with water. Hence, it is soluble in water. But aniline does not undergo H-bonding with water to a very large extent due to the presence of a large hydrophobic -CH group. Hence, aniline is insoluble in water.

steps.description: Explain the H-bonding capability of ethylamine.
Discuss the hydrophobic nature of aniline.

parts.final_answer: Thus, ethylamine is soluble in water while aniline is not.

parts.part_text: Methylamine in water reacts with ferric chloride to precipitate hydrated ferric oxide.
parts.answer_text: Due to the +I effect of -CH3 group, methylamine is more basic than water. Therefore, in water, methylamine produces OH- ions by accepting H+ ions from water. Ferric chloride (FeCl3) dissociates in water to form Fe3+ and Cl- ions. Then, OH- ion reacts with Fe3+ ion to form a precipitate of hydrated ferric oxide.

steps.description: Explain the basicity of methylamine in water.
Describe the reaction between OH- ions and Fe3+ ions.

parts.final_answer: Thus, methylamine reacts with ferric chloride to precipitate hydrated ferric oxide.

parts.part_text: Although amino group is o, p- directing in aromatic electrophilic substitution reactions, aniline on nitration gives a substantial amount of m-nitroaniline.
parts.answer_text: Nitration is carried out in an acidic medium. In an acidic medium, aniline is protonated to give anilinium ion (which is meta-directing). For this reason, aniline on nitration gives a substantial amount of m-nitroaniline.

steps.description: Explain the effect of acidic medium on aniline during nitration.

parts.final_answer: Thus, aniline gives a substantial amount of m-nitroaniline upon nitration.

parts.part_text: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.
parts.answer_text: A Friedel-Crafts reaction is carried out in the presence of AlCl3. But AlCl3 is acidic in nature, while aniline is a strong base. Thus, aniline reacts with AlCl3 to form a salt. Due to the positive charge on the N-atom, electrophilic substitution in the benzene ring is deactivated. Hence, aniline does not undergo the Friedel-Crafts reaction.

steps.description: Explain the nature of AlCl3 and its reaction with aniline.
Discuss the deactivation of electrophilic substitution in aniline.

parts.final_answer: Thus, aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.

parts.part_text: Diazonium salts of aromatic amines are more stable than those of aliphatic amines.
parts.answer_text: The diazonium ion undergoes resonance, which accounts for the stability of the diazonium ion. Hence, diazonium salts of aromatic amines are more stable than those of aliphatic amines.

steps.description: Explain the resonance in diazonium ions.
Discuss the stability of diazonium salts.

parts.final_answer: Thus, diazonium salts of aromatic amines are more stable than those of aliphatic amines.

parts.part_text: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is preferred for synthesising primary amines.
parts.answer_text: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis results in the formation of 1° amine only. 2° or 3° amines are not formed in this synthesis. Thus, a pure 1° amine can be obtained. Therefore, Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is preferred for synthesizing primary amines.

steps.description: Explain the outcome of Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
Discuss the purity of the amines obtained.

parts.final_answer: Thus, Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is preferred for synthesizing primary amines.

question_text: Describe a method for the identification of primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Also write chemical equations of the reactions involved.

question_image.description: Diagrams illustrating the reactions of primary, secondary, and tertiary amines with Hinsberg's reagent.

answer_text: Primary, secondary and tertiary amines can be identified and distinguished by Hinsberg's test. In this test, the amines are allowed to react with Hinsberg's reagent, benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl). The three types of amines react differently with Hinsberg's reagent. Therefore, they can be easily identified using Hinsberg's reagent. Primary amines react with benzenesulphonyl chloride to form N-alkylbenzenesulphonyl amide which is soluble in alkali. Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to give a sulphonamide which is insoluble in alkali. Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent at all.
final_answer: Thus, Hinsberg's test allows for the identification of primary, secondary, and tertiary amines based on their reactivity with benzenesulphonyl chloride.

question_text: Write the reactions of (i) aromatic and (ii) aliphatic primary amines with nitrous acid.

question_image.description: Diagram showing the reaction of aromatic amines with nitrous acid forming diazonium salts.

answer_text: (i) Aromatic amines react with nitrous acid (prepared in situ from NaNO2 and a mineral acid such as HCl) at 273 - 278 K to form stable aromatic diazonium salts i.e., NaCl and H2O. (ii) Aliphatic primary amines react with nitrous acid (prepared in situ from NaNO2 and a mineral acid such as HCl) to form unstable aliphatic diazonium salts, which further produce alcohol and HCl with the evolution of N2 gas.
final_answer: Thus, aromatic amines form stable diazonium salts while aliphatic amines form unstable ones that decompose.
